definitions.explanation: Causing an uncomfortable, unsettling feeling. Describes something that feels wrong or sinister in a way that is hard to explain.

examples.japanese: {気味悪|きみわる}い{音|おと}がする。
あの{廃墟|はいきょ}は{気味悪|きみわる}い{雰囲気|ふんいき}だ。
examples.english: That ruin has an eerie atmosphere.

examples.japanese: {誰|だれ}もいないはずの{部屋|へや}から{足音|あしおと}が{聞|き}こえて{気味悪|きみわる}かった。
examples.english: I heard footsteps from a room where nobody should be, and it was creepy.

notes:
FORMS:
・Adverbial: {気味悪|きみわる}く
・Noun form: {気味悪|きみわる}さ

CONJUGATION:
・Negative: {気味悪|きみわる}くない
・Te-form: {気味悪|きみわる}くて
・Past: {気味悪|きみわる}かった

VARIANT READING:
Also read as きびわるい in some regions, but きみわるい is standard.

SIMILAR WORDS:
・{気味悪|きみわる}い vs. {怖|こわ}い — {気味悪|きみわる}い emphasizes an uncanny, unsettling quality, while {怖|こわ}い is general fear
・{気味悪|きみわる}い vs. {不気味|ぶきみ} — {不気味|ぶきみ} (na-adjective) is similar in meaning and more commonly used in formal writing
